summary: Reviewed all 9 standard figures on the run 15 (5 GeV LuAG anchor) page against the STD captions in build_runbook.py (lines 37-64). Verdict: 4 of 9 captions have real caption-vs-content mismatches, three of them major-to-critical because the STD caption is reused verbatim on every run page while run 15's figures show superseded working points. NEW findings (not in FINDINGS.md): (1) MCPThreshold caption quotes "final working point 137 mV" while the run 15 figure itself is annotated "turn-on: 976 ADC-eq = 238 mV" — the old threshold this very run was taken at (critical for reader trust; run 15's electron sample is the trigger-sculpted one). (2) XCETCheck caption promises "coincidence rate vs software threshold... set on the coincidence plateau" but the macro (macros/XCETCheck.C, TCanvas Divide(2,1)) only draws the two amplitude spectra — the coincidence scan is printf'd to stdout, never drawn; worse, the drawn "current 150 ADC-eq cut" line is the superseded threshold FINDINGS proved clips ~9% of 5 GeV electrons (adopted plateau value is 100). (3) QCv2_align caption promises "row/column balance" but QCv2.C's cA canvas is Divide(2,1) — the balance numbers (rows 1.255±0.014, cols 0.909±0.010) exist only in QCv2_summary.txt; the drawn right panel also has no legend and clipped pad titles. (4) BestTiming caption says "Median combination adopted; mean kept alongside for comparison," yet the figure draws ONLY the mean combination (248±8 ps core fit) — the adopted median estimator appears nowhere, and the number a reader takes away is not the number feeding the campaign trend (389/sqrt(E)+138 → ~312 ps at 5 GeV). Secondary caption overreach: QCv2_MIP's "absorbs day-scale gain drift" is exactly the claim the documented noise-estimator-bias finding qualifies; ElectronID's "carries selection to energies the XCETs cannot reach" is stale since the hardware tag was shown to work at 9/11 GeV (runs 28/30). Physics questions the team can answer from existing data: the coherent −1.2 ns satellite shoulder in all four capillaries (documented as open — select bump events and inspect TR0 waveforms); TR0 channels' post-pulse +500 ADC-eq baseline band with median peak-sample ~50 sitting near the baseline window (possible baseline-window contamination of the timing reference); EMPTY channels 9-12 having the highest rail fraction in Integrity_health; XCET40 vs XCET43 pe-yield asymmetry quantifiable from the visible 1-pe spike at ~55 ADC-eq (predicts floor-tag efficiency at 9/11 GeV); the near-zero discrimination of the max LG/ΣLG "shower sharing" ElectronID variable; and contamination of the off-coincidence training sample with real electrons at run 15's electron-rejecting 240 mV MCP threshold.

plots.what_it_shows: 18-pad grid of per-channel waveform persistence maps (log color), one pad per DRS4 channel, with the teal mean tagged-electron waveform overlaid. Channel map readable at a glance: 0 XCET40, 1 XCET43 (small negative pulses ~sample 420-450), 2 ScintA (negative, large spread), 3/9/10/11/12 EMPTY (flat), 4-7 LG 4-7 (positive, very slow — peak ~sample 300-400, i.e. ~60-80 ns, decaying past sample 1000), 8/17 TR0 g0/g1 (sharp negative spike at ~sample 50 followed by a persistent positive band at ~+500 ADC-eq), 13-16 HG(5)/HG(4)/HG(7)/HG(6) (positive, fast, peak ~sample 60-80, visibly noisy ±1000 baselines — the daytime-noise era).
plots.caption_issues: Caption (build_runbook.py lines 37-39) is accurate and matches the drawn content: per-channel overlay, log color, teal mean tagged-electron waveform, and it delivers on 'channel identity, polarity, timing windows, dead/noisy channels'. Nit: 'Every event in the run' — pads are visibly downsampled/persistence-binned, not literally every trace, but that is conventional.
plots.design_issues: Minor: the HG channel labels use the paired-capillary convention 'HG(5)' etc. while LG pads say 'LG 4' — fine for insiders but the swap (13=HG(5), 14=HG(4), 15=HG(7), 16=HG(6)) is exactly the pairing pitfall the integrity checks exist for; a one-word 'pairing verified' stamp on the pad would close the loop. Nit: EMPTY pads waste a third of the canvas.
plots.physics_questions: NEW: (1) TR0 g0/g1 show a persistent positive band at ~+500 ADC-eq spanning the full window after the pulse — either a real post-pulse overshoot/undershoot-inverted recovery or baseline-window contamination: with the TR0 median peak sample at ~50 (see Integrity_health, near the lower dashed guide at ~30), events where the MCP pulse intrudes on the baseline-estimation window would shift the whole subtracted trace up by exactly this kind of offset. Since TR0 is the campaign time reference, the team should check whether the srCFD reference time correlates with this offset (existing data, one afternoon). (2) LG pulses peak ~60-80 ns after HG pulses from the same SiPM — a huge shaping difference between the two gain paths; worth one line in documentation because it explains why timing must come from HG with LG only supplying the amplitude prediction. (3) Channel 3 (EMPTY) shows sporadic dots around sample 400-600 — crosstalk pickup worth a 5-minute look given it shares the group with the XCETs/ScintA.

plots.what_it_shows: Four summary panels vs channel number 0-17: baseline RMS (log y; ~2-5 ADC-eq for XCET/LG, ~80-110 for HG 13-16 — the documented daytime run 15 noise), signal fraction with amp>150 (ch 2 ScintA 0.88, ch 8 TR0 ~1.0, LG 4-7 ~0.2, HG 13-17 pegged at ~1.0), rail fraction (log y; peak values 3e-3 to 7e-3 on channels 9-12, ~1e-3 on LG, ~1e-4 low outliers at 8 and 17), and median pulse-peak sample with dashed red guide lines at ~30 and ~990 (TR0 channels ~50, XCETs ~420-500, LG ~370-400, HG ~180-230).
plots.caption_issues: Caption (lines 40-42) correctly names all four drawn panels. Minor overreach: 'Event gaps and rails surface here first' — no event-gap panel exists in this figure (gaps live in Integrity_summary.txt); only rails surface here. Minor: 'median pulse peak-time' is actually in samples, not time — the axis says sample; nit-level unit sloppiness.
plots.design_issues: Minor: the signal-fraction metric is saturated/meaningless for the HG channels in this run — amp>150 against a baseline RMS of 80-110 ADC-eq means noise alone fires the metric, so HG 'signal fraction' ~1.0 carries no information precisely in the daytime runs where you'd want it; a threshold scaled to per-channel RMS (e.g. 5×RMS) would restore meaning. Minor: no channel-name labels on the x axes (reader must cross-reference the waveform grid to know 13=HG(5)).
plots.physics_questions: NEW: the four EMPTY channels 9-12 have the HIGHEST rail fraction on the canvas (3e-3 to 7e-3, an order of magnitude above the LG channels the caption calls the watch item). Unterminated DRS4 inputs picking up spikes, or a rail-counting artifact on near-zero baselines? Cheap to answer from existing waveforms, and it matters because the same rail counter feeds the LG bias-headroom watch item — if it triggers on glitches in empty channels it may over- or under-count real LG rails. Known/documented: the HG RMS 81-111 for run 15 vs 50-55 overnight (lighting leak + thermal) is already in FINDINGS.md.

plots.what_it_shows: 2x2 grid of off-coincidence HG amplitude spectra (log y, 0-2000 ADC-eq) with Landau fits drawn from ~230 to ~900-1050 ADC-eq. All four capillaries peak near 350-450 ADC-eq (consistent with the documented run 15 MIP scale ~404 and the day-scale gain ladder 404→327→281→216 across runs 15/24/27/28). Above ~1100 every panel shows a roughly flat tail at 10-30 events/bin extending to 2000.
plots.caption_issues: Caption (lines 43-45) is accurate on the sample and fit family, but two problems. Major (staleness/overreach): 'The MIP MPV is the per-run gain reference that absorbs day-scale gain drift' — FINDINGS.md documents that part of the apparent day-scale ladder is a noise-estimator bias (daytime baseline RMS ~2x inflates the amplitude-based MPV) and that the MIP estimator 'should use charge integrals or noise-robust fits when baseline RMS is elevated'; per-run MIPs remain operative but do NOT cleanly absorb the drift, and cross-run MIP normalization was proven invalid (species + noise bias). The caption sells the strong version of the claim the campaign log has already walked back. Minor: no fit range, MPV values, or convention stated in the caption, and the drawn fits stop around 900-1050 with no explanation of the truncation.
plots.design_issues: Major (legibility): the pad titles are clipped at the top of the canvas — the capillary identity of each panel is unreadable in the rendered PNG, so the '2x2 grid per capillary' cannot actually be mapped to capillaries 4/5/6/7 from the figure alone (the sibling TransferFit figure does this correctly with in-pad labels). Minor: MPV values are not annotated on the panels even though they are the single number the figure exists to deliver; reader must go to QCv2_summary.txt.
plots.physics_questions: NEW: (1) the flat high tail above ~1100 ADC-eq in all four off-coincidence spectra — at run 15's 240 mV MCP threshold the trigger preferentially rejected electrons (documented), so untagged electrons and showering hadrons plausibly populate this tail; does the Landau MPV shift if the fit window or sample is tightened (e.g. requiring MIP-like ΣHG/ΣLG)? This directly feeds the MIP-vs-noise-estimator question already open in FINDINGS. (2) The fits visibly undershoot the data in the 700-1000 region of the upper-left panel — is the Landau-only model (no Gaussian convolution?) biasing the MPV by a few % differently per channel? Cheap refit from existing histograms.

plots.what_it_shows: Top row: per-capillary (4/5/6/7, labeled in-pad) HG peak spectra for beam events, log y, with the measured clip wall drawn as a solid red line (~3143/3170/3117?/3186 — red text partially legible, matches FINDINGS 3143-3186) and the 0.72×wall fit cutoff as an orange dotted line (~2270). Bottom row: HG vs LG 2D scatter with profile points, teal linear fit (HG = 301+2.39·LG, 280+2.50·LG, 204+2.66·LG, 226+2.83·LG), dashed extrapolation, red clip-wall line, and the fit region shaded (fit: LG 30-815/805/795/695, HG < 0.72 wall) with a proper legend.
plots.caption_issues: Caption (lines 46-49) is accurate: fit restricted below the wall, fit range drawn explicitly, purpose (predicting true amplitude of clipped pulses) correct, matching FINDINGS numbers exactly. Minor incompleteness: the caption never mentions the top row (the per-capillary wall measurement spectra), the 0.72×wall criterion, or the per-cap LG windows — the '0.72' appears only inside the figure. Nit: 'no clipped high-gain signal is ever discarded' is a pipeline claim, not something this figure demonstrates.
plots.design_issues: This is the best-designed figure of the nine (explicit fit region, legend, in-pad parameters). Minor: the red 'wall NNNN' labels in the top row collide with the dotted line and are partly illegible at published resolution; move to the stats corner. Minor: bottom-row shading encodes only the LG range — the HG < 0.72·wall part of the cut is not visually distinguishable from the LG cut.
plots.physics_questions: NEW: (1) transfer slopes span 2.39→2.83 (+18%) across the four capillaries — is this SiPM-to-SiPM gain-ratio spread or channel shaping differences? A cross-check against the MIP MPV ratios per channel would separate optical from electronic differences using existing data. (2) All four intercepts are positive and large (204-301 ADC-eq at LG=0): what breaks proportionality at small amplitude — LG threshold/peak-finder bias on small pulses, or the LG/HG shaping difference seen in the waveform grid? This matters because the srCFD threshold is 0.15× the LG-PREDICTED amplitude: for small pulses the intercept dominates and the predicted amplitude (hence CFD threshold) is systematically off. (3) Capillary 5 shows a coherent population BELOW the extrapolation at LG 850-1200 (HG under-responding before the wall) while cap 7's scatter sits above — residuals vs LG per capillary would reveal whether the linear extrapolation biases clip-recovered amplitudes at the high-energy scan points, which feeds the ~13.6k LG headroom discussion.

plots.what_it_shows: Two panels: TR0 group 0 (0-4000 ADC-eq) and TR0 group 1 zoom (0-2000), log y MCP peak-amplitude spectra with a red vertical line annotated 'turn-on: 976 ADC-eq = 238 mV'. Sharp trigger cliff at 976; spectrum extends to ~3600 (g0). A handful of sub-threshold entries at ~830-960 and a spike of ~10 events at zero amplitude.
plots.caption_issues: CRITICAL (stale working-point number vs figure content): caption (lines 50-52) states 'Final working point 137 mV — low enough to keep the smaller electron pulses (the old 240 mV rejected them)', but this run 15 figure is annotated 238 mV — run 15 WAS taken at the old, electron-rejecting threshold (sequence 240→164→137 mV across runs 15/22/23, FINDINGS.md lines 275-292). On the run 15 page the STD caption reads as if the drawn measurement should be 137 mV; a reader who checks the plot sees 238 and concludes either the caption or the plot is wrong. The caption needs a per-run number (or wording like 'this run's measured threshold is annotated; campaign working point converged to 137 mV from run 23'). This matters physically: run 15 anchors the calibration yet its electron sample is the trigger-sculpted one (9.1% coincidence vs 21.8% at 137 mV). Minor: 'trigger turn-on' — no turn-on/efficiency curve is drawn, only the spectrum edge with a line.
plots.design_issues: Minor: the second panel is labeled '(zoom)' but is a different channel (group 1) at a different range — the label conflates channel and range. Minor: no edge-width annotation (FINDINGS quotes ~7 mV) and no marker for the mean pulse amplitude, which is what makes the 65%-of-mean sculpting argument visible.
plots.physics_questions: NEW: (1) the ~10 events at exactly zero MCP amplitude and the handful at 830-960 (below the hardware threshold) — how did these events trigger? Candidates: trigger fired on the OTHER TR0 copy (copies differ event-by-event), peak-finder picking the wrong excursion, or non-TR0 trigger contamination. Since these are reference-less or weak-reference events entering the timing sample, one afternoon with existing waveforms settles it and defines a clean MCP-quality cut. (2) Does the MCP reference jitter differ between the 238 mV runs (large-pulse-only reference, better MCP resolution) and the 137 mV runs? The diagonal-difference ref-jitter estimate (107-114 ps) was validated on LuAG runs — checking it separately for run 15 vs runs 23+ would tell whether the trend's +138 ps floor mixes two reference qualities. Known/documented: the electron-rejection sculpting itself and the offline MCP-amplitude cut recommendation are already in FINDINGS.

plots.what_it_shows: Two panels: XCET 40 and XCET 43 amplitude spectra (log y, 0-600 ADC-eq), each labeled '(0.21 bar)', with a dashed vertical line labeled 'dashed: current 150 ADC-eq cut'. Both show a pedestal spike near 0, a narrow secondary spike at ~55 ADC-eq (single-pe candidate), a valley, and a broad electron band: XCET40's band runs ~150 to beyond 600, XCET43's is narrower, peaking ~250-300 and dying by ~450-500.
plots.caption_issues: MAJOR (caption promises a panel that is not drawn): caption (lines 53-55) says 'Cherenkov photoelectron spectra AND coincidence rate vs software threshold. The electron-tag threshold is set on the coincidence plateau, per energy.' The macro (macros/XCETCheck.C) computes the 6-point threshold scan but only printf's it — TCanvas c.Divide(2,1) draws just the two spectra; no coincidence-vs-threshold graph exists in any run's version of this figure. MAJOR (stale annotation contradicting the caption's own convention): the drawn 'current 150 ADC-eq cut' is the superseded common threshold — the XCET threshold audit (FINDINGS.md, 'XCET threshold audit across the scan') showed 150 clips ~9% of 5 GeV electrons (this run's energy) and the adopted per-energy plateau thresholds are {100,100,100,50}. So the caption asserts plateau-based per-energy thresholds while the run 15 figure draws the retired 150 line. Either draw the adopted threshold per run or relabel the line 'historical 150 cut (superseded)'.
plots.design_issues: Minor: adding the printed coincidence-vs-threshold scan as a third pad (or an inset TGraph) would make the figure self-consistent with its caption at zero analysis cost — the numbers are already computed in the same macro. Minor: no pe-yield annotation despite '(0.21 bar)' implying ~5 pe.
plots.physics_questions: NEW: (1) the two counters are visibly asymmetric — XCET40's electron band extends past 600 ADC-eq while XCET43's ends by ~450-500 with a lower valley: different pe yields or PMT gains. The clean ~55 ADC-eq single-pe spike visible in BOTH panels gives a free gain calibration: dividing the band mean by the 1-pe peak yields pe/counter, from which Poisson zero-fractions predict per-counter and coincidence tag efficiency vs pressure — directly testable against the measured floor-tag rates at 9 GeV (~3 pe, 4.86%) and 11 GeV (2.17%), and it would quantify how many real electrons the 9/11 GeV floor tags miss. (2) What is the ~55 ADC-eq spike population physically in-run — genuine 1-pe from below-threshold particles (mu/pi scintillation contamination in the gas/windows) or after-pulsing? A coincidence test between the two counters' 1-pe populations answers it from existing data.

plots.what_it_shows: Three normalized-comparison panels, XCET-tagged electrons (red filled) vs off-coincidence (blue): 'shower sharing' max LG/ΣLG (both peak at ~0.30 with nearly identical shapes), 'prompt/slow balance' ΣHG/ΣLG (electrons narrow at ~3, off-coincidence broad 4-7 — the working discriminant), and 'total LG energy' ΣLG (off-coincidence spiked at ~300 MIP-like with 30% in one bin; tagged electrons a low flat continuum to ~2000 plus a broad shower peak ~3300).
plots.caption_issues: Minor-to-major staleness: caption (lines 56-58) says the selector 'carries the electron selection to beam energies the XCETs cannot reach' — that was the pre-scan plan (offline ID for 7/9/11 GeV). The campaign outcome, documented in FINDINGS and in the run 30 notes ('the hardware tag works after all... ElectronID cross-checks the tag instead of replacing it'), is that the XCET tag worked at every energy including 11 GeV; ElectronID's actual role is cross-check/tag-and-probe. The caption on every production run page states a purpose the campaign retired. Minor: caption calls off-coincidence 'hadrons' — at run 15's 240 mV MCP threshold the off-coincidence sample demonstrably contains trigger-surviving untagged electrons, so the label overstates purity. Minor: 'tag-and-probe' is named but no efficiency, working points, or cut lines appear in the figure.
plots.design_issues: Minor: no cut/selector lines drawn on any panel, so the 'selector' cannot be read off the figure; the 83.2% efficiency quoted in later run notes has no visual anchor. Minor: 'prompt / slow balance' as a name for ΣHG/ΣLG is opaque — HG and LG see the same light with different shaping; a one-word note on why this ratio separates species (amplitude-weighting of fast component) belongs in the caption.
plots.physics_questions: NEW: (1) the shower-sharing variable max LG/ΣLG shows essentially zero separation between tagged electrons and off-coincidence — why is it in the selector at all, and what drives both species to the same 0.30 sharing? For a 2x2 sampling of shower max, MIP-like hadrons should share differently than showers unless the LG slow shaping integrates enough that sharing is geometry- not species-dominated. Worth checking whether dropping it changes the quoted 83.2% efficiency. (2) The blue off-coincidence ΣLG distribution has a non-negligible shoulder overlapping the electron peak region (2500-4000) — consistent with real electrons in the 'hadron' sample at run 15's sculpting threshold; the team can bound the training-sample contamination by re-deriving the templates from a low-MCP-threshold run (23+) and comparing selector boundaries. This propagates into the tag-and-probe efficiency systematics quoted downstream.

plots.what_it_shows: Two panels. Left: tagged-electron ΣLG spectrum (linear y, 0-4500) with a low-side spike at ~130 ADC-eq (the module-miss population), a flat continuum, and a broad contained-shower peak at ~3200. Right: log-y overlay of five per-channel pulse peak-time (sample) distributions in red/green/blue/black/grey — green spikes at ~50 (TR0-like), black narrow at ~450, tall grey narrow at ~510, blue broad at ~430, red essentially FLAT at ~100 counts/bin across the entire 0-1024 window.
plots.caption_issues: MAJOR (caption promises content not drawn): caption (lines 59-61) lists 'row/column balance' as part of the figure, but macros/QCv2.C draws canvas cA with Divide(2,1) — only the ΣLG spectrum and the peak-time overlay. The row/column numbers exist solely in QCv2_summary.txt (run 15: rows bottom/top = 1.255 ± 0.014, cols left/right = 0.909 ± 0.010). So the alignment claim in the caption cannot be verified from the figure on any run page. Minor: 'pulse peak-time containment' is a stretch for the right panel as drawn — with no legend it does not demonstrate containment of anything to a reader.
plots.design_issues: MAJOR (legibility): the right panel has NO legend — five colored histograms with unidentifiable channels; the red flat distribution (a channel whose peak-finder lands uniformly at random, i.e. noise-dominated in most events) is uninterpretable without knowing which channel it is. Both pad titles are clipped at the canvas top (same defect as QCv2_MIP). The information content of this panel is currently near zero for anyone but the author. Adding the missing third pad (row/col balance) and a legend would fix caption and figure simultaneously.
plots.physics_questions: Known/documented but visually hidden: the run 15 row asymmetry 1.255 ± 0.014 (bottom/top) is the residual ~1-2 mm offset flagged after the run 14 stage move ('optionally nudge ~1 mm further down') — since the campaign has no tracker and σ/E is position-smearing dominated everywhere, this 25% row imbalance at the anchor run is exactly the quantity the missing panel should display. NEW: (1) which channel is the red flat peak-time distribution, and is its flatness expected (an LG channel where most triggers have no signal above the peak-finder floor)? If it is an LG channel, the LG peak-time is meaningless for most events and any peak-time-window cut built on it behaves differently per channel. (2) The left spectrum's miss spike at ~130 plus flat continuum to ~2000: the miss fraction can be read off per run and compared to the row/col imbalance — a self-consistency check on the no-tracker alignment story available from existing summaries.

plots.what_it_shows: Left: per-capillary srCFD Δt−median vs TR0, four overlaid histograms with legend σ values cap4 375, cap5 408, cap6 312, cap7 356 ps (matches FINDINGS 312-409), all four showing a coherent satellite shoulder at ~−1.0 to −1.3 ns at the few-percent level plus flat far tails. Right: '4-capillary MEAN shower time' with an iterative-core Gaussian fit, σ = 248 ± 8 ps annotated '(incl. MCP+DRS)'.
plots.caption_issues: MAJOR (caption inverted relative to content): caption (lines 62-64) says 'Median combination adopted; mean kept alongside for comparison' — but the figure draws ONLY the mean combination; the adopted median estimator appears nowhere on the canvas. On every run page the sole timing figure headline (here 248 ± 8 ps) is the estimator the campaign explicitly rejected after runs 30/32 showed the mean is destroyed by outliers (11 GeV: median 227 vs mean 547; DSB1 9 GeV: 133 vs 516). For run 15 (clean conditions) mean≈median presumably, but the figure gives no evidence of that, and the number feeding the campaign trend (389/√E+138 → ~312 ps at 5 GeV, median convention, ref included) is not derivable from the drawn 248 ps core-fit σ — a reader comparing figure to scan page hits an unexplained 248-vs-312 discrepancy (different estimator AND different fit convention). Minor: the caption's srCFD threshold description omits the guards (>20 mV, <0.9×wall) documented in FINDINGS; the fit convention for the quoted σ (iterative Gaussian core? robust tebSigma?) is stated neither in caption nor on the plot.
plots.design_issues: Minor: add the median-combination histogram (or at least its σ) to the right panel — one line of macro code reconciles figure, caption, and scan page. Minor: the left-panel legend σ values' estimator (fit vs robust width) is unstated. Nit: the Gaussian fit visibly excludes the −1 ns shoulder; a fit-range indication would make the core-fit convention honest.
plots.physics_questions: Documented-but-open (FINDINGS flags it 'worth understanding before the scan analysis' and it remains unresolved): the ~−1.2 ns satellite shoulder. NEW sharpening from this figure: the shoulder is COHERENT across all four capillaries at the same Δt — a per-capillary optical effect (e.g. direct Cherenkov in the capillary vs scintillation) would not line up identically in all four, so the culprit is event-level or reference-side: an early second beam particle in the same bucket structure (T10 RF ~1 ns spacing?), an MCP after-/pre-pulse population, or a DRS4 wrong-cell pathology. Concrete existing-data tests: select shoulder events and (a) inspect TR0 waveforms for double pulses, (b) check their MCP amplitude and the zero/sub-threshold MCP population from MCPThreshold.png, (c) check ScintA amplitude (two particles → double MIP deposit). Second question: does the shoulder fraction scale with beam intensity across runs (pile-up signature) — answerable from the registry's rate data. Third: quantify mean-vs-median agreement for THIS clean run to certify the trend's 5 GeV point uses a consistent convention.
